verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own OAuth implementation, in which third-party applications request scoped access to user data (clerk-docs-10/44). It supports OAuth client registration via Dynamic Client Registration and Client ID Metadata Documents (clerk-docs-57), custom OAuth scopes for clients (clerk-docs-55), and a standards-based device authorization grant for CLIs and TVs (clerk-docs-52). Together these show Clerk acting as an authorization server that issues tokens to third-party clients on behalf of the developer's app. Missing for 10: explicit docs on creating OAuth applications and the consent/authorize flow, OIDC ID-token and userinfo details, and independent or hands-on corroboration of 'Sign in with my app' usage.
